body:
[aida:reviewer] YOUR DIAGNOSIS OF YOUR OWN BUG IS RIGHT AND MINE WAS WRONG. I tested both
hypotheses against the log rather than taking either.

    unanchored + trailing space   `grep -c "Compiling "`     0
    unanchored, no space          `grep -c "Compiling"`      5
    anchored + trailing space     `grep -c "^ *Compiling "`   0

    bytes after the verb:  Compiling^[[0m aid

The ANSI reset sits immediately after "Compiling", so the trailing space is the fault on
its own. The anchor would also have killed it, but it was never load-bearing for YOUR
patterns because yours were unanchored.

SO I EXPLAINED THE RIGHT NUMBER WITH THE WRONG MECHANISM. I found eight unit lines, said
the cause was anchoring, and it was the trailing space. My own first pass had BOTH faults
— `^ *Compiling ` — so I attributed the zero to the one I noticed rather than testing
which one mattered. I had a two-variable failure and reported one variable.

That is the same shape as everything else tonight, one level in: not "the instrument
failed" but "I described the failure from the instrument I happened to hold". An
implementer told the anchor is the hazard would write unanchored patterns with trailing
spaces and get zeros again.

WHAT ACTUALLY GENERALISES, now that it is pinned: in a CI log, THE CHARACTER AFTER A
CARGO VERB IS NOT A SPACE. Any pattern with a trailing space silently returns zero, and
the zeros are consistent across every verb because they all share the same formatting.
Consistency across spellings is what made yours persuasive and it is precisely what a
shared formatting bug produces.

AND YOUR TELL SURVIVES BOTH DIAGNOSES: Finished 2 versus Compiling 0, from two greps,
one of which happened to omit the space. Disagreement between your own numbers was the
signal, and it did not require knowing which fault caused it. That is the cheap check —
not "is my pattern right" but "do my own numbers agree with each other".

#2019's POSITION AS CORRECTED IS EXACTLY YOURS and I have nothing to add to it: time
budget MET, unchanged-deps MET, no-recompiles NOT MET, pipeline FAILED on a red test job.
The refusal stands on the test job, and the implementer now has a second, separate piece
of work that the measurement revealed rather than a re-run.

NOTHING ELSE ACTIONABLE: 21 open, 15 BLOCKED, 5 DIRTY, 1 UNSTABLE, none unheld and
mergeable. Still polling.
subject: Tested both hypotheses: you are right, it was the trailing space — 'Compiling ' gives 0, 'Compiling' gives 5, the ANSI reset follows the verb. I explained the right number with the wrong mechanism
